purpose: the device integrator is live now; this records the last correctness bug found in it and the accuracy that results

the_bug.wrong: rsa_g = (ktau > s.rsa_ktau) & (k > s.rsa_kmin), and likewise rsa_r with s.rsa_ktau_nu - constant thresholds
the_bug.right: CAMB switches to the algebraic streaming form at tau > max(15/k, taurend), i.e. k*tau > max(15, k*taurend) (equations.f90:313-323). The numpy solver already used max(s.rsa_ktau, k*c['taurend']); the port had never been brought across.
the_bug.effect: a constant threshold fires EARLY, so the port entered the RSA branch while numpy was still integrating the hierarchy
the_bug.how_it_was_found: a and-by-a comparison of numpy vs torch rhs at eight scale factors, with both absolute and relative criteria. Rows of order 1e-58 had been dismissed as noise earlier; the real signal was in dr, the massless-neutrino density, where the relative difference reached 1.7e+01 at a=1e-3 and 1.0e+00 at a=1e-2, then vanished entirely by a=0.05
the_bug.why_it_hid_for_so_long: at a=0.05 and a=0.3 the two sides agree to 0.000e+00, because by then both are fully inside the RSA branch and dr takes the same algebraic form. Every earlier correctness check ran at a=0.05, i.e. entirely inside the region where the bug is invisible.

the_fix_effect.steps_unchanged: 8330 both before and after, so the step limiter was already right - only the rhs regime test was wrong

two_more_bugs_fixed_in_the_same_pass.bug: a was carried as np.where(done, a, ...), so on the final step it stopped a few ulp short of a_end. The output test a_out[j] <= a_now then never fired and rec stayed at its initial NaN - which looked exactly like a diverged run but was a bookkeeping bug.
two_more_bugs_fixed_in_the_same_pass.fix: pin a to a_end when done, plus a post-loop fill as a safety net

two_more_bugs_fixed_in_the_same_pass.bug: none; added an optional check_every so a mid-run non-finite state can be located instead of only being visible at the end

what_is_now_true.device_integrator: evolve_torch_adaptive advances the whole batch by min over trajectories of the numpy step limiter, ported to the device as elementwise where/min/clamp over the coefficient tensors
what_is_now_true.accuracy_at_k_0.3: 3.718e-06 relative against the numpy solver, over a full 8330-step integration
what_is_now_true.schedule: identical step count to numpy, so the limiter port is exact
what_is_now_true.the_tight_coupling_era: the earlier 0.26% relative disagreement at a=1e-7 on 1e-58 states is still present and still judged as numerical noise; it does not affect the result

caveats: k=0.3 verified; the k=0.9 half of the same run had not reported when this was written
one trajectory, one cosmology; nothing here is a batched measurement
the 7.3% step penalty of batch-uniform stepping was measured on the numpy side, not on the device
no end-to-end nonlinear number and no GPU speedup is claimed
the_pattern_worth_noting: this is the fifth bug in this session that lives only in the ported/device path and is invisible in the default configuration: _taurend_nu truncated by zip(), _tau_end built per-cosmology, tau_rem broadcasting to (T,T), the two missing massive-neutrino masks, and now the constant RSA threshold. Every one of them was hidden by bucket_by_k running T=1 (for the first four) or by checking only at late times (for this one).
